records.label: A sourced public history of Maddela

data.overview: Maddela's civic story begins before the modern municipality, in a landscape shaped by Indigenous communities, river valleys, forests and later migration. A local compilation records settlement and road-building stories from 1919 and the 1920s; these are presented as local tradition, while laws and institutional sources anchor the documented milestones that followed.

sections.title: Communities, migration and Pinappagan
sections.text: A local historical compilation describes Ilongot or Bugkalot and Dumagat communities in the wider area, then an Ilocano settlement effort led by forester Vicente Velasco in 1919 at a place called Pinappagan. Because the compilation does not cite archival records for every name and date, BetterMaddela attributes this account rather than treating it as a controlling legal history.

sections.title: The documented municipal reorganization
sections.text: Executive Order No. 368 reorganized municipalities and municipal districts in Nueva Vizcaya, included Maddela among ten municipalities, defined its historical boundary and took effect immediately. The order is the clearest recovered legal milestone for Maddela's modern municipal status; it does not itself prove an exact Pinappagan renaming date.

sections.title: Maddela becomes part of Quirino
sections.text: Republic Act No. 4734 included Maddela in the Subprovince of Quirino in 1966. Republic Act No. 5554 amended that arrangement in 1969, and Republic Act No. 6394 provided for Quirino's separation from Nueva Vizcaya as a regular province in 1971. The laws' plebiscite conditions are preserved without inventing results not stated in the inspected texts.

sections.title: Territorial change and Nagtipunan
sections.text: Batas Pambansa Blg. 345 provided for thirteen barangays then within Maddela to form the Municipality of Nagtipunan, subject to a plebiscite. This later territorial change is why Maddela's 1950 historical boundary and area are not presented as its current geography.

sections.title: A protected landscape
sections.text: Proclamation No. 548 established the Quirino Protected Landscape across portions of Maddela and other municipalities. Its landscape-wide area is not a measure of Maddela's municipal land area.

sections.title: A rural municipality shaped by farms, learning and nature
sections.text: Maddela is a first-income-class municipality of 32 barangays with an official 2024 population of 41,867. Public institutions and sources connect its present identity with agriculture, Quirino State University's campus in Dipintin, the protected landscape and destinations such as Governor's Rapids and Maddela Waterfalls. These are source-scoped descriptions, not promotional rankings.

data.publicationNote: Local tradition and documented legal fact are intentionally distinguished. No single unsupported founding or renaming date, current land area, visitor schedule or tourism safety claim is inferred.

records.notes: This narrative complements, and does not replace, the existing record-level legal instruments.

records.label: Barangay officials for all 32 Maddela barangays, including Sangguniang Kabataan councils and appointed officers, as listed by the DILG Barangay Officials Profiling System (retrieved 2026-08-28)
records.notes: Owner approved publication on 2026-08-28 in the project review conversation, including official office email addresses and shared telephone numbers. The Region 2 masterlist export supplied by the owner the same day extends the listing with SK members, treasurers and secretaries, and adds the source's TERM column; it also lists three officials twice (published here once) and carries a lost-character marker in 23 cells, restored to Ñ as described in the listing basis. The earlier barangay-officials evidence round (2026-08-26) could not verify any punong barangay; the DILG BOPS listing independently corroborates its single weak lead (Pedro Blanza Salvador, Diduyon).

data.listingBasis: Names, positions, term ordinals and telephone numbers are reproduced verbatim from the DILG Barangay Officials Profiling System Region 2 masterlist export (official-list_02_2026-08-28.xlsx, 42,919 rows, TERM column 2023 - 2026), filtered to QUIRINO / MADDELA: 633 rows, published here as 630 officials after removing three exact duplicate rows (Mae Ann Pedronan Bueno, Cofcaville SK member; Irish Pearl Jamias Joguilon, Manglad SK member; Arnel Ramos Ambrocio, San Bernabe sangguniang barangay member). The export carries a lost-character marker (U+FFFD) in place of Ñ in 23 cells: the 19 Santo Niño barangay cells and the names of Fredireck Leaño and Recto Leaño are restored to the spelling used by the system's own web listing, while Jay-Ar Leaño (San Pedro SK member) and Noemi Maraña (Villa Hermosa Sur treasurer) are restored contextually because the web listing does not cover those roles. Official office email addresses appear only in the system's web listing and are cross-referenced from it; every web row matches exactly one masterlist row. Personal names are composed by concatenating the dataset's separate first-name, middle-name, last-name and suffix fields in that order; no other rewriting was applied.
data.termBasis: The masterlist TERM column states 2023 - 2026 for every listed official; officials elected at the October 30, 2023 BSKE appear to hold over through the barangay and SK elections reportedly scheduled for November 2, 2026 (secondary, unofficial source; COMELEC confirmation not yet retrieved). Term-in-present-position ordinals are reproduced where the source states them (blank for appointed treasurer and secretary roles). The listing is re-checked monthly and will be re-verified against the next barangay election results.
data.limitations: Names are reproduced verbatim in the source's uppercase styling; mid-term appointments or replacements may not be reflected. Telephone numbers are shared barangay office lines (13 distinct numbers across the 66 entries that carry one), so a number identifies the barangay office rather than an individual official. Email addresses are published for 23 of 630 officials; all other contact values are absent at source (N/A, NONE, or blank markers) and are shown as not published. The source publishes no photographs of officials.

data.method: Raw OpenStreetMap place-node coordinates (never interpolated), matched to the reviewed 32-name PSGC list. No administrative boundary polygons exist in OpenStreetMap for Maddela, so positions are points, not shapes. Nine barangays have no barangay-level OpenStreetMap feature and are listed as unmapped; nearby POIs such as schools or cemeteries were not used as barangay coordinates.

records.label: Province boundary polygons for mainland Luzon from OCHA COD-AB, used only for the stylized Luzon locator map

data.attribution: Administrative boundaries © UN OCHA Philippines COD-AB, CC BY-IGO 3.0
data.method: Province polygons from the same OCHA COD-AB Philippines geodatabase (v03, features valid on 2025-02-13) used for the Maddela atlas, phl_admin2 layer. Mainland Luzon covers Regions I, II excluding Batanes, III, CAR, NCR, IV-A excluding island provinces, and V excluding Catanduanes and Masbate, as directed by the owner. The four NCR district rows are merged into a single Metropolitan Manila feature. Geometry is simplified at 0.012 degrees with islets under 0.015 degrees of bbox diagonal dropped for stylized web rendering. Maddela is rebuilt from the reviewed municipal atlas geometry and re-projected into the same frame: its centroid sits within 2 km of the COD-AB municipal center and its area computes to 773 versus 770.62 square kilometers. Not an official survey boundary.
